historical_growth.growth_rate_source: explicit driver path (guidance-led): FY2026 adjusted-sales guidance 0% to -6% CER, then MFN/IRA price resets and the 2031-32 semaglutide patent cliff. Average base revenue growth over the 10-year path is ~0-1%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (25-32%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue/EPS CAGR (19-24%) and is NOT a usable forward rate: it reflects the 2021-24 GLP-1 boom plus debt-funded Catalent and Akero deals. All trailing growth series are backward-looking peak-cycle numbers; the company now guides flat-to-negative adjusted sales for FY2026.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (-23.9% 3y, -1.0% 5y) sit roughly level with reported FCF CAGRs, so SBC is not eating the growth (SBC ~0.5% of revenue). The FCF collapse is capex-driven: PP&E capex rose from DKK 7bn (FY2021) to ~60bn (FY2025) for API and fill-finish capacity, plus lumpy intangible purchases (DKK 16.3bn FY2020, 13.1bn FY2023, 30.0bn FY2025). Excluding intangibles the owner-FCF series is 45.3bn (FY2020) -> 65.2bn (FY2022) -> 57.5bn (FY2025).

scenario_narratives.base: Novo remains a GLP-1 co-leader behind Lilly. FY2026 lands near the guidance midpoint on adjusted sales (-3.5% DKK); the Wegovy pill and Wegovy HD carry volume while MFN, the 2027 IRA Medicare price and the Jan-2027 WAC cuts keep realised prices falling, giving low-single-digit growth to 2030. The DKK 8bn transformation savings are largely reinvested, holding EBITDA margins ~46%. Capex falls from ~DKK 55bn as the capacity build completes. The 2031-32 semaglutide patent expiry costs ~10% of revenue over two years and margins settle at 40%; CagriSema/amycretin and the Akero MASH asset partly backfill. Terminal value is capped at 14x FCF, a post-LOE big-pharma multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Wegovy pill becomes the dominant oral obesity therapy, the US Bridge/Medicare coverage expansion turns the MFN price cut into a net volume unlock, and ex-US pill launches across 30+ markets drive 6-8% growth in 2027-30. Amycretin succeeds in phase 3 and arrives before the semaglutide cliff, so the 2031-33 LOE only flattens revenue. Margins recover toward 49-50% on cost discipline and stay ~46% after the cliff.
scenario_narratives.bear: Lilly's tirzepatide and next-gen orals (orforglipron, retatrutide), plus Pfizer/Metsera and Amgen, take share; CagriSema and amycretin keep underwhelming; realised prices keep sliding under MFN/IRA and international semaglutide generics spread market by market (as in Canada in 2026) well before 2031. Revenue falls 6% a year in 2026-27 and the US/EU LOE in 2031-33 removes ~20% more. Margins compress to 33% as fixed manufacturing capacity is under-utilised (the 2026 right-sizing charges are the early sign) and R&D spend is held up to rebuild the pipeline. GLP-1 product-liability litigation is a further tail not separately modelled.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the cash a DKK-reporting pharma company generates through a known patent cliff, on an owner basis (SBC expensed, intangible in-licensing charged as capex), discounted at a DKK WACC with all molecule, pricing and competition risk carried in three scenarios rather than in the discount rate. The FY2025 owner FCF of DKK 27.6bn is a trough distorted by a DKK 30bn intangibles spike and peak PP&E capex; the build starts from adjusted sales and margins, not from that FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Semaglutide exclusivity erodes earlier or faster than the 2031-32 dates (Canada lost it in Jan 2026)
Further US price resets beyond MFN/IRA, or Medicare Bridge coverage not delivering volume
Tirzepatide and next-gen oral/amylin competitors take more share than the base case assumes
Pipeline failures (CagriSema, amycretin) leave nothing to backfill the cliff
Capex does not decline as guided, or capacity is stranded (further right-sizing charges)
USD/DKK: about half of sales are US; a weaker USD lowers DKK flows and the USD value per ADR moves with the rate
GLP-1 product-liability MDL and IT-security class actions

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NVO, NYSE, USD); 52-week range 35.12-64.16. FX from Yahoo DKK=X; parity vs NOVO-B.CO in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: NVO_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, DKK millions, text-extracted from 20-F/6-K; SEC XBRL currency mislabelled USD and not used); 6-K Q2-2026 (H1 2026 cash flow, net debt reconciliation, FY2026 guidance); 6-K Q4-2025 (FY2025 sales and 340B adjustment).

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average share count implied by H1 2026 diluted EPS (net profit DKK 69,546m / DKK 15.66 = ~4,441m), 6-K Q2-2026. 1 ADR = 1 B share. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the DKK 15bn 2026 buyback (DKK 7.5bn executed by 3 Aug 2026) is the cash mechanism that funds employee-share transfers and cancels shares, so a falling count would double-credit it. Post 2:1 split (Sept 2023) basis throughout.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments, FY2025 consolidated statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back (DKK 1,435m). Novo settles awards from treasury shares bought in the market, so there is no separate net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 across the history).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury-share purchases DKK 1,388m (buyback paused during the 2025 Akero/Catalent-era leverage); H1 2026 DKK 5,899m under the DKK 15bn 2026 programme. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fx_note: Model flows in DKK; NYSE ADR quoted in USD, 1 ADR = 1 B share. fx_rate = 1 / USDDKK 6.6421 (Yahoo Finance DKK=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-03T21:00Z) = 0.150555 USD per DKK. Parity check: Copenhagen NOVO-B.CO DKK 248.75 (close 2026-10-02) / 6.6421 = USD 37.45 within 0.35% of the NYSE NVO close at inputs.price_as_of, confirming rate, direction and 1:1 ratio. refresh_price.py moves the USD price but not this rate; re-date the rate when refreshing.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in DKK, the flows' currency. Risk-free: Danish 10y government ~2.6% (DKK pegged to EUR, ~Bund +10bp). ERP 5.5%, beta 0.85 (large-cap pharma, raised from the ~0.6 long-run pharma beta for the 2025-26 GLP-1 volatility) -> cost of equity ~7.3% + 0.4pp for concentration in one molecule family = ~7.7%. Debt (AA/Aa3, EUR 15bn + CHF 1.09bn bonds) ~3.0% pre-tax, 2.3% after tax, at ~8% of EV. WACC ~7.5%, identical across scenarios: patent-cliff, pricing and competition risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities DKK 8,622m (30 Jun 2026) are included in total_debt (borrowings 121,794 + 18,333 = 140,127 incl. leases) and lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation and the capex path carries lease-asset renewal. Leases are ~0.3% of revenue, immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material -- Novo Nordisk A/S consolidates wholly owned subsidiaries; no NCI line in equity.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF (component route, make build-dcf) with the non-US adaptations, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US'. Novo is an operating pharma company with real free cash flow; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no MEMORY entry). BASE REVENUE: FY2025 ADJUSTED sales DKK 306,400m = reported 309,064m less the USD 0.4bn (~DKK 2.7bn) Q2 2025 340B provision reduction that management excludes from adjusted sales (6-K Q4-2025 line 812). The Q1 2026 DKK 26.8bn 340B reversal is non-cash and non-recurring and is excluded from every projected year -- the growth path compounds from adjusted sales, so no one-off reversal is extrapolated. CAPEX DEFINITION: the CSV CapEx column INCLUDES purchase of intangibles (FY2025 90,113 = PP&E ~60,140 + intangibles 29,973; H1 2026 24,840 = 23,986 + 854), contrary to the parser note. Reported FCF 28,989 is therefore after the ~DKK 30bn FY2025 intangibles spike (Akero/Omeros in-licensing), and owner FCF 27,554 is a trough, not a mid-cycle base; ex the intangibles spike FY2025 owner FCF was ~57.5bn. The projected capex path carries PP&E (guided ~55bn 2026, 'expected to decline in the coming years') plus ~1-1.5% of revenue of ongoing business-development intangibles, because a pharma company must buy pipeline to replace semaglutide. YEAR-1 CHECK: base FY2026 owner FCF builds to ~DKK 53bn vs company FCF guidance of 45-55bn (OCF less PP&E capex; interest now in financing). TIMING: fy0 is FY2025 and year 1 is FY2026, but net debt is the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, which already holds the H1 2026 FCF retained after DKK 41.2bn of H1 distributions (~DKK 14bn, ~DKK 3/share, <2% of value) -- a small, stated double count, preferred to using the Dec-2025 balance sheet which would credit holders with DKK 35bn of dividends already paid away. Interest income not stripped: Novo is net debt (DKK 86.5bn ex leases), so interest_income = 0. Not an SBC-zero market but SBC is only ~0.45% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -3.5% in DKK on adjusted sales: guidance 0% to -6% CER, ~1pp worse in DKK (midpoint -4%), nudged toward the upper half because guidance has been raised three times and H1 adjusted sales were -2% DKK. FY2027 +1%: Jan-2027 WAC cuts and the IRA Medicare negotiated semaglutide price offset by Bridge/Medicare obesity coverage and Wegovy pill volume. FY2028-30 +3-4%: GLP-1 volume expansion and ex-US pill launches against falling realised prices. FY2031-33: semaglutide compound patents expire 2031-32 in US/EU/Japan (Canada and parts of International already lost exclusivity in 2026); peptide generics erode more slowly than small molecules and CagriSema/amycretin partially replace, so -6% and -4% rather than a cliff. Then low growth.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 48.4% after ~DKK 8bn transformation costs; FY2024 50.8%. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA ~49.6% before ~DKK 3bn one-off capacity right-sizing costs and a guided H2 step-up in R&D and promotion. 47% for 2026, ~46% while price resets bite and DKK 8bn of savings are reinvested, then down to 40% post-LOE (big-pharma steady state is ~35-40%).
base.capex_rationale: Includes intangible purchases (the CSV CapEx definition). PP&E capex guided ~DKK 55bn in 2026 (vs 60bn 2025) and 'expected to decline in coming years'; PP&E is now DKK 232bn so depreciation rises as capacity comes online. Steady state 8% = ~6.5% PP&E maintenance + ~1.5% recurring in-licensing/BD, vs D&A 7%.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Guided ETR 21-23%; Danish statutory 22%. FY2026 at 24% for the cash-tax lag (FY2025 taxes paid DKK 32.0bn on higher prior-year profit).
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + inventory exceed payables for a pharma manufacturer, so growth consumes cash (capture negative); US rebate-accrual timing makes the actual swings lumpy (H1 2026 WC -19.9bn).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the franchise rests on one molecule family with a dated patent cliff, the pipeline has missed repeatedly (CagriSema, ZEUS, monlunabant impairment) and a single regulator (US pricing policy) has already reset prices once. Base 50% is the guidance-anchored path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: pill dominance, the coverage-for-price trade turning net positive, and a pipeline success landing before 2031.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
